items.q: Stakeholder map shows: Shareholders (high power, low interest), Employees (high power, high interest), Suppliers (low power, low interest), Customers (low power, high interest). Which is most likely to influence decisions?
opts: Suppliers
Customers
Shareholders
Employees
items.why: Employees have high power and high interest, placing them in the 'Key Players' quadrant - the most influential position. Read the specific map given. In this business, employees have both high power and high interest.
items.label: Past paper question

items.q: A 'hard' approach to HRM would:
opts: Focus on efficient use of capital equipment
Treat employees as a resource to be used as efficiently as possible
View workers as a valuable asset to be developed
Focus solely on better recruitment methods
items.why: Hard HRM treats employees as a resource (like any other factor of production) to be used efficiently and cost-effectively. Soft HRM views them as valuable assets to be developed and empowered. Hard HRM = resource (cost focus, control, efficiency). Soft HRM = asset (development, trust, empowerment).
items.label: Past paper question

items.q: Primark's corporate objective is to maximise sales volume through low prices. Which of the following best describes how a functional objective should relate to this corporate objective?
opts: The marketing department should set an independent objective focused on brand prestige.
The operations department should set a functional objective to minimise unit production costs.
The HR department should set a functional objective to maximise employee pay.
The finance department should set a functional objective to maximise profit margins on each product line.
items.why: Functional objectives must support the corporate objective. If the business competes on low prices and high volume, operations minimising unit costs directly enables this. Maximising profit margins per product (option 4) conflicts with a low-price, high-volume strategy, and brand prestige (option 1) contradicts Primark's positioning.
items.label: New question

items.q:
Statement 1: Monetary policy refers to government decisions on taxation and public spending.

Statement 2: A cut in interest rates is an example of expansionary monetary policy, intended to stimulate economic activity.
opts: Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is true.
Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is false.
Statement 1 is false. Statement 2 is true.
Statement 1 is false. Statement 2 is false.
items.why: Statement 1 is false: taxation and public spending decisions are fiscal policy; monetary policy concerns the money supply and interest rates (set by the Bank of England). Statement 2 is correct: cutting interest rates reduces the cost of borrowing, encouraging spending and investment, which is expansionary. This is one of the most commonly confused pairs of economic concepts.
items.label: New question

items.q: The government announces a significant increase in corporation tax. Which of the following describes the most direct impact on a profitable UK business?
opts: The cost of borrowing for the business will increase.
The business will have less retained profit available to reinvest after tax.
Consumer demand for the business's products will immediately fall.
The exchange rate will weaken, reducing the business's export competitiveness.
items.why: Corporation tax is levied on profits, so a higher rate directly reduces post-tax (retained) profit available for reinvestment or dividends. The cost of borrowing is set by monetary policy (interest rates), not corporation tax. Changes in consumer demand and exchange rates are indirect, second-order effects, not the most direct impact on the business itself.
items.label: New question

items.q:
Statement 1: A business's strong brand reputation is classified as an opportunity in a SWOT analysis.

Statement 2: High staff turnover within a business is classified as a weakness in a SWOT analysis.
opts: Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is true.
Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is false.
Statement 1 is false. Statement 2 is true.
Statement 1 is false. Statement 2 is false.
items.why: Strengths and weaknesses are internal factors. A strong brand is internal, so it is a strength, not an opportunity — Statement 1 is false. High staff turnover is an internal problem, correctly classified as a weakness — Statement 2 is true. The most common error is placing internal factors in the external categories.
items.label: New question

items.q:
Statement 1: Cost-push inflation occurs when rising production costs, such as energy or wages, force firms to raise their prices.

Statement 2: High inflation always increases a firm's profitability because revenue rises faster than costs.
opts: Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is true.
Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is false.
Statement 1 is false. Statement 2 is true.
Statement 1 is false. Statement 2 is false.
items.why: Cost-push inflation is correctly defined in Statement 1. Statement 2 is false because during cost-push inflation costs rise faster than or at the same rate as revenue, potentially squeezing profit margins. Even demand-pull inflation does not guarantee profit growth if competition prevents firms from raising prices sufficiently.
items.label: New question

items.q: Which statement about integration is true?
opts: Backward vertical integration is impossible for a retailer.
Conglomerate integration narrows the product range.
Forward vertical integration gives better access to raw materials.
Horizontal integration gives an immediate increase in market share.
items.why: Horizontal integration (buying a competitor) immediately gives you their customers and market share. A is wrong (retailers can integrate backward to wholesalers/manufacturers). B is wrong (conglomerate widens range). C describes backward, not forward. Buying a competitor = instant market share gain. This is horizontal integration's primary advantage.
items.label: Past paper question

items.q: Which one of the following external factors is most likely to cause an increase in demand and a decrease in costs for a highly geared furniture retailer?
opts: New competition entering the market
Increases in incomes for all workers in the country
A decrease in the rate of interest
A fall in the number of people of working age
items.why: Lower interest rates: (1) Increase demand - consumers afford mortgages, driving furniture purchases. (2) Decrease costs - business is highly geared (lots of debt), so lower rates reduce interest payments significantly. It means lots of debt, so interest rate changes have a big impact on costs.
items.label: Past paper question

items.q: Statement 1: 'In a very centralised organisation, local managers decide store design.' Statement 2: 'In a decentralised organisation, local managers decide inventory items.'
opts: Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is true.
Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is false.
Statement 1 is false. Statement 2 is true.
Statement 1 is false. Statement 2 is false.
items.why: Statement 1 false - in a centralised organisation, head office makes decisions like store design, not local managers. Statement 2 true - in a decentralised organisation, local managers have authority to make decisions like choosing inventory. Centralised = head office decides. Decentralised = local managers decide.
items.label: Past paper question

items.q: GreenBuild Ltd has recently carried out a rebranding exercise, repositioning itself as a premium sustainable construction firm. Which of the following best explains why this would require the finance department to revise its functional objectives?
opts: The finance department must reduce its overall budget allocation and redirect all discretionary spending towards the new marketing and branding campaign activities.
A change in corporate strategy alters the financial targets and investment priorities needed to support the new direction.
Functional objectives across all departments, including finance, are determined independently of wider corporate strategy and are unaffected by rebranding decisions.
The rebranding will automatically increase revenue and improve profit margins, meaning financial targets will be met without any revision to existing objectives.
items.why: Functional objectives must align with and support changes in corporate strategy. A shift to premium positioning changes investment needs, pricing strategies and return expectations, so finance must revise its objectives accordingly. Option 3 is a common misconception; option 4 ignores the need for planned, coordinated targets.
items.label: New question

items.q: A business helps its local community to improve quality of life. In Carroll's pyramid, this is:
opts: Economic responsibility
Ethical responsibility
Legal responsibility
Philanthropic responsibility
items.why: Philanthropic responsibility sits at the top of Carroll's pyramid - it's about giving back to the community and being a good corporate citizen. It goes beyond legal and ethical obligations to actively help society. Carroll's pyramid bottom to top: Economic, Legal, Ethical, Philanthropic. Community improvement = philanthropic (voluntary giving back).
items.label: Past paper question

items.q: Which is an example of monetary policy to help businesses expand?
opts: Discouraging banks from lending
Lower corporation tax rates
Increased government subsidies
Lower interest rates
items.why: Lower interest rates = monetary policy (controlled by central bank). Corporation tax and subsidies are fiscal policy. Discouraging lending would hinder expansion. Monetary policy = interest rates and money supply. Fiscal policy = taxation and government spending.
items.label: Past paper question

items.q: Which of the following statements is true?
opts: An increase in interest rates is likely to lead to more demand for houses.
The population size is a demographic factor in the external environment.
A soft approach to human resource management is likely to involve a low level of delegation.
A mission will have a more specific target than a business objective.
items.why: Population size is a demographic factor. A is false (higher rates = less housing demand). C is false (soft HRM = high delegation). D is false (objectives are more specific than missions). Soft HRM = trust, delegation, empowerment. Hard HRM = control, cost minimisation.
items.label: Past paper question

items.q: Statement 1: 'Improving quality makes demand more price elastic.' Statement 2: 'Improving quality increases added value.'
opts: Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is true.
Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is false.
Statement 1 is false. Statement 2 is true.
Statement 1 is false. Statement 2 is false.
items.why: Statement 1 is false - improving quality makes demand more price inelastic (not elastic) because customers become more loyal and less sensitive to price. Statement 2 is true - better quality allows higher prices and/or creates a perception of greater worth, increasing value added. Quality improvement = more brand loyalty = less price sensitivity = more inelastic.
items.label: Past paper question

items.q:
Statement 1: A mission statement is a measurable, time-specific target that guides short-term decision-making.

Statement 2: Corporate objectives are derived from the mission statement and give the organisation a more precise sense of direction.
opts: Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is true.
Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is false.
Statement 1 is false. Statement 2 is true.
Statement 1 is false. Statement 2 is false.
items.why: A mission statement is a broad statement of purpose and values, not a measurable target — that description fits an objective. Corporate objectives are indeed derived from the mission and give more specific direction, so Statement 2 is correct. Students often confuse mission statements with SMART objectives.
items.label: New question

items.q:
Statement 1: Big data refers specifically to data sets that are stored in a single, centralised database owned by the firm.
Statement 2: Data mining allows businesses to identify patterns in large data sets that can be used to predict future consumer behaviour.
opts: Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is true.
Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is false.
Statement 1 is false. Statement 2 is true.
Statement 1 is false. Statement 2 is false.
items.why: Big data is characterised by large volume, variety and velocity of data from multiple sources — it is not defined by being centralised in a single database, so Statement 1 is false. Data mining is precisely the process of analysing large data sets to extract patterns and insights that can inform decisions such as targeting customers, making Statement 2 true.
items.label: New question

items.q: Jenson Ltd has just hired a team of recently qualified graduates with little industry experience. According to the Tannenbaum Schmidt continuum, which approach would be most appropriate for their line manager?
opts: Delegate decisions entirely and allow the team to set their own objectives, deadlines, and working methods without managerial interference
Consult the team extensively before making any decision, giving equal weight to each graduate's opinion regardless of their limited experience
Retain a high degree of authority, telling the team what to do with limited discussion
Allow the team to operate within broad limits defined by the manager, giving them freedom to decide how best to achieve targets within those boundaries
items.why: The Tannenbaum Schmidt continuum suggests that the appropriate style depends partly on subordinates' experience and competence. Inexperienced graduates require more direction from the manager, placing the style towards the 'tells' end of the continuum where managerial authority is high. Full delegation or broad-limits approaches suit experienced, capable teams. Students sometimes confuse 'tells' with negative or demotivating management.
items.label: New question

items.q: Employees 100 to 120, leavers 20 to 22, output 1000 to 1150. What happened between 2013 and 2014?
opts: LP increased and turnover increased
LP increased and turnover decreased
LP decreased and turnover increased
LP decreased and turnover decreased
items.why: LP: 2013 = 1000/100 = 10. 2014 = 1150/120 = 9.58. decreased. Turnover: 2013 = 20/100 = 20%. 2014 = 22/120 = 18.3%. decreased. Both decreased. The calculations are identical. Always compute rather than guess.
items.label: Past paper question

items.q: Monarch Engineering exports 70% of its output to the eurozone, invoicing customers in euros. If the pound strengthens significantly against the euro, which of the following is most likely to occur?
opts: Monarch's euro-denominated revenues will convert to more pounds, increasing profitability.
Monarch's products will become relatively cheaper for eurozone customers, boosting demand.
Monarch's pound-equivalent revenues will fall, potentially reducing profit margins.
Monarch will benefit because its imported raw material costs will rise.
items.why: A stronger pound means each euro converts to fewer pounds, so euro revenues buy less sterling — pound-equivalent revenues fall. This squeezes margins unless costs also fall proportionally. Option 1 is the reverse of what happens. Option 2 is the effect of a weaker pound, not a stronger one.
items.label: New question
